classification.difficultyReason: Follow explicit integration and landing-time scaffolds, then use impact velocity components and rationalisation to establish the supplied direction.

content.prompt:
A stone is thrown from the top of an $11\text{ m}$ high vertical tower.
The initial speed is $12\text{ m/s}$ and the initial direction is $30^\circ$ below the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Starting with the horizontal and vertical components of acceleration, show that $\dot{x}=6\sqrt{3}$ and $\dot{y}=-10t-6$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\ddot{x}&=0,\qquad \ddot{y}=-10\\\dot{x}&=C_1,\qquad \dot{y}=-10t+C_2\\\dot{x}(0)&=12\cos30^\circ=6\sqrt{3}\\\dot{y}(0)&=-12\sin30^\circ=-6\\\dot{x}&=6\sqrt{3}\\\dot{y}&=-10t-6\end{aligned}$$
The initial vertical velocity is negative because the stone is thrown downwards.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the origin is at the point of projection, find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $t$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x&=6\sqrt{3}\,t+C_3\\y&=-5t^2-6t+C_4\end{aligned}$$
At the point of projection, $x(0)=y(0)=0$, so $C_3=C_4=0$.
$$\begin{aligned}x&=6\sqrt{3}\,t\\y&=-5t^2-6t\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: How long does it take for the stone to hit the ground?

answer.worked:
At ground level, $y=-11$.
$$\begin{aligned}-11&=-5t^2-6t\\5t^2+6t-11&=0\\(5t+11)(t-1)&=0\\t&=-\frac{11}{5}\quad\text{or}\quad t=1\end{aligned}$$
Reject the negative time. The stone hits the ground after $1\text{ s}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: How far from the base of the tower does it land (to $1$ d.p.)?

children.label: e
children.prompt: Show the stone hits the ground at an angle of $\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{9}\right)$ below the horizontal.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\dot{x}(1)&=6\sqrt{3}\\\dot{y}(1)&=-10-6=-16\\\tan\theta&=\frac{16}{6\sqrt{3}}\\&=\frac{8}{3\sqrt{3}}\\&=\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{9}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{9}\right)\end{aligned}$$
The vertical velocity is negative, so this angle is below the horizontal.
